question: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2024, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**9 August 2024.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Carriage of Goods by Sea Bill, 2024, was introduced to modernize and streamline the existing laws governing maritime transport.
 
• The Bill aims to replace the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925, aligning India’s maritime laws with international standards.
 
• It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on August 9, 2024, to address current challenges and ensure a robust legal framework for sea transport.
 
• This Bill facilitates the carriage of goods by sea, ensuring the protection of interests of all parties involved, including shippers, carriers, and consignees.
 
• The introduction of this Bill marks a significant step in enhancing the efficiency and competitiveness of India's maritime sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maritime Law:**

 
 
• Maritime law, also known as admiralty law, is a body of laws, conventions, and treaties that govern private maritime business and other nautical matters.
 
• It covers a wide range of issues including shipping, navigation, waters, insurance, and the conduct of seamen.
 
 
 
• **International Maritime Organization (IMO):**
 
 
• The IMO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for regulating shipping.
 
• Its primary purpose is to develop and maintain a comprehensive regulatory framework for shipping, including safety, environmental concerns, legal matters, technical cooperation, maritime security, and the efficiency of shipping.
 
 
 
• **Bill of Lading:**
 
 
• A Bill of Lading is a document issued by a carrier to acknowledge receipt of cargo for shipment.
 
• It serves as a shipment receipt when the carrier delivers the goods at a predetermined destination.
 
• It is a legally binding document between the shipper and the carrier detailing the type, quantity, and destination of the goods being carried.
 
 
 
• **Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925:**
 
 
• The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 1925, is an Act of the Parliament of India which regulates the rights and responsibilities of shippers and carriers involved in the carriage of goods by sea.
 
• It was based on the Hague Rules, which were developed to create a uniform legal regime for the international carriage of goods by sea.
 
• The Act established the liabilities of carriers and the rights of shippers, providing a legal framework for addressing disputes and claims arising from maritime transport.
